data.title: Manchester United Posts Wider Loss as Managerial Change Comes Amid Struggling Performance
data.description:
By Freddy Sebastian

Manchester United posted a wider loss in its fiscal first quarter as the men's first team sits near the bottom of the Premier League standings, facing a potential relegation battle almost midway through the season.

The results come about a week after the club hired former U.S. national team manager Mauricio Pochettino, who guided the Americans through the World Cup on U.S. soil in the summer. The Argentine replaced former United midfielder Michael Carrick after the men's side plunged to 18th place in the table.

For the fiscal first quarter, Manchester United, the 13-time Premier League champions, posted a loss of GBP18.1 million ($23.8 million), compared with a loss of GBP6.6 million the year before. On an adjusted basis, loss was GBP13.3 million in the latest period.

Revenue rose 4.1% to GBP146.1 million, helped by a 17.7% growth in broadcasting revenue, driven by the team's participation in UEFA's Champions League competition during the current year. Commercial revenue slipped 0.1%, while matchday revenue rose 2.3%.

Sponsorship revenue fell 3%, mostly because of a shorter pre-season tour before the 2026/2027 campaign due to the World Cup. Retail, merchandising, apparel and product licensing revenue climbed 3.5%.

The club still expects fiscal-year revenue of GBP740 million to GBP760 million, along with adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of between GBP205 million and GBP225 million.

Pochettino led Southampton in the early 2010s before taking over as manager for Tottenham, which he lead to a Champions League final. Since then, he has managed Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the American national team.

"We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch," Manchester United Chief Executive Omar Berrada said Thursday.

Shares fell nearly 8% to $20.20 in premarket trading.

Write to Freddy Sebastian at freddy.sebastian@wsj.com

data.title: Marsh's Oliver Wyman To Acquire Synpulse
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Oliver Wyman, a management consulting firm and a business of Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc. (MRSH), said Thursday that it has agreed to acquire Synpulse, a technology consulting and AI platform company serving financial services organizations.

Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Marsh said the acquisition will combine Oliver Wyman's strategy consulting capabilities with Synpulse's technology and implementation expertise to help banks, insurers and asset managers with business transformation.

'Synpulse brings exceptional technology consulting and AI engineering capabilities, deep financial services expertise and a track record of delivering complex enterprise change,' said Ted Moynihan, President and CEO of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027.

In pre-market trading on the NYSE, Marsh shares were up 0.66% after closing at $205.43 on Wednesday.

data.title: TGT Stock Gets Multiple Price-Target Hikes — But Guggenheim Says Turnaround Still Has To Prove Itself
data.description:
Key points:
  • Piper Sandler raised its price target on Target to $176 from $153 while maintaining a ‘Neutral’ rating, citing strong third-quarter results and healthy comparable sales but expressing uncertainty over Target’s 2027 sales trends, according to The Fly.
  • Baird also raised its price target to $180 from $175 while maintaining a ‘Neutral’ rating, saying that the retailer was well positioned for the holiday season, TheFly reported.
  • Thirteen of 39 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy,’ while 22 rate it ‘Hold’ and four rate it ‘Strong Sell,’ according to Koyfin.

Target Corp. (TGT) shares drew investor attention on Thursday after multiple analysts raised their price targets on the stock, even as Guggenheim cautioned that further gains will depend on continued sales growth and stronger earnings.

Guggenheim raised its price target on TGT to $180 from $175 while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating, adding that investors still want to see more evidence of a sustained turnaround, according to TheFly. The revised target implies an upside potential of 8.5% from TGT stock’s last close.

TGT shares traded marginally lower in premarket trading on Thursday at the time of writing.

Analyst Views Diverge On TGT

Separately, Piper Sandler raised its price target on Target to $176 from $153 while maintaining a ‘Neutral’ rating, according to TheFly. The revised target implies around 6.1% upside potential from the stock’s last close.

The firm cited Target’s strong third-quarter results, healthy comparable sales growth and earnings upside. However, it expressed some uncertainty about the company’s comparable sales trends in 2027, while adding that improving category trends were encouraging, according to TheFly.

Baird also raised its price target to $180 from $175 while maintaining a ‘Neutral’ rating, according to TheFly. The revised target implies about 8.5% upside potential from the stock’s last close. The firm updated its model following Target’s third-quarter results and said the retailer was well positioned for the holiday season.

Similarly, Jefferies raised its price target on the stock to $195 from $190, while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating. The revised target implies around 17.5% upside potential from the stock’s last close. The firm also pointed to improving November sales trends compared with October, which strengthened its confidence in Target’s holiday-season outlook, according to the note published by Investing.com.

Thirteen of 39 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy,’ while 22 rate it ‘Hold,’ and four rate it ‘Strong Sell,’ according to Koyfin.

Q3 Earnings Recap

Target reported third-quarter net sales of $27.1 billion, up 7.1% year over year, while comparable sales increased 5.6%, driven by a 5% rise in traffic. Digital comparable sales grew 9.8%, compared with 4.6% growth in stores.

Adjusted earnings-per-share (EPS) came in at $2.65, including a $0.50 benefit from tariff refunds. Excluding the refunds, adjusted EPS increased 21% year over year. Target also raised its full-year sales growth outlook to around 6% and its EPS guidance to $10.65 to $11.40, including around $2.14 in tariff refund benefits.

How Retail Views TGT

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

data.title: India allows older vessels into fleet to cut reliance on foreign carriers
data.description:
By Nidhi Verma

India has relaxed rules allowing vessels more than 20 years old to be registered under its flag, according to a government order, potentially expanding its domestic shipping fleet and reducing reliance on foreign carriers

  • The new rules lay out conditions for 15- to 20-year-old oil tankers to join the Indian registry or avail themselves of the Indian flag, said the order by the federal maritime agency, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA)

  • For vessels above 20 years of age, including oil tankers, general cargo vessels and offshore fleet entry into the Indian flag registry requires approval by a five-member committee of DGMA to ensure the quality of ships

  • There are no exit age limits for Indian-flag ships, said the order issued on Wednesday

  • Previously, vessels older than 20 years were not permitted to register under the Indian flag

  • India, a key consumer of oil, gas and other products, largely relies on foreign carriers for imports

  • The move will improve India's access to ships in times of crisis

  • Indian-flagged vessels get priority in securing certain government and state-run companies' cargo contracts before foreign-flagged ships are considered

data.title: Marsh’s Oliver Wyman to Acquire Financial Services and Technology Consultancy Synpulse
data.description:
Oliver Wyman, a global leader in management consulting and a Marsh business (), today announced an agreement to acquire Synpulse, a global technology consulting and AI platform company serving banks, insurers, wealth managers and other financial services organizations. Terms of the deal, expected to close in early 2027, were not disclosed.

Banks, insurers and asset managers face significant changes driven by advances in technology, data and AI, as well as evolving business models. As these changes accelerate, clients are looking for partners who can help them navigate every stage of transformation, from strategy to technology implementation and execution. Oliver Wyman and Synpulse have already been working together with combined teams on multiple end-to-end transformations for our clients. The acquisition will enable the two businesses to continue to work closely together, combining complementary capabilities and teams to service clients across strategy, technology and implementation.

Synpulse brings technology experience that helps financial institutions modernize legacy systems, improve operations and respond to changing client needs. Through responsible AI strategy and digital ecosystem transformation, Synpulse helps clients bring new products to market faster, simplify operations, and deliver more personalized customer experiences.

“Our clients don’t separate strategy from technology and execution—they need great ideas to deliver real change,” said Ted Moynihan, President and CEO of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting. “Synpulse brings exceptional technology consulting and AI engineering capabilities, deep financial services expertise and a track record of delivering complex enterprise change. Together, we will deliver a winning combination of talent and technology to help clients achieve their biggest ambitions.”

“Since our founding in 1996, Synpulse has built a strong position as a trusted partner to financial institutions in their digital transformations,” said Konrad Niggli, Co-CEO of Synpulse. "Working alongside Oliver Wyman will enable us to support our clients across the entire digital and AI transformation journey, from strategy through implementation and execution. It gives us greater scale to deepen the value we bring to our clients.”

“Bringing our teams together creates opportunities to expand our reach across markets, take on larger and more complex transformation projects, and accelerate our growth across regions. It also strengthens our ability to invest in AI and technology, further enhancing the capabilities we bring to our clients,” said Yves Roesti, Co-CEO of Synpulse.

Upon closing, Synpulse’s approximately 1,200 employees will continue to operate from offices in North America, Europe and Asia. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

About Oliver Wyman

data.title: IndiGo expands South East Asia connectivity
data.description:
IndiGo is increasing its flights to South East Asia with new services to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

The airline will introduce a new daily flight between Delhi and Kuala Lumpur from December 20 and increase frequencies from the national capital to Bangkok and Singapore. It will also launch a flight between Bengaluru and Hanoi in Vietnam from December 20.

The capacity expansion, which is expected to push tourism, comes as India announced free e-visas for citizens of ASEAN member countries.

IndiGo operates over 50 weekly flights connecting Delhi to Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam and Indonesia. “The addition of Kuala Lumpur to Delhi’s network, along with increased frequencies to Singapore and Bangkok, further reinforces Delhi’s position as a key international hub while deepening connectivity between India and South East Asia’s leading travel, business and trade markets,” the airline said on Thursday.

data.title: Karnataka to establish Government sports technology CoE with Amagi Media Labs
data.description:
The Government of Karnataka has signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with Amagi Media Labs Limited to establish a Sports Technology Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, envisioned as India’s first government Sports Technology Centre of Excellence, bringing together technology, research and industry expertise to strengthen the sporting ecosystem.

The initiative aims to advance the application of technology in sports and support the development of Karnataka’s sporting ecosystem. Speaking at the press conference, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Electronics, IT & BT and e-Governance, Government of Karnataka, said the sports ecosystem, valued at approximately $41 billion, is expected to grow by 12–15 per cent in the coming years, making it an important opportunity for Karnataka.

The proposed centre will be structured around three major pillars — Core Technology and Research Areas, Athlete Development, and Cross-Cutting Ecosystem Enablers — bringing together technological innovation, scientific approaches to athlete development and industry collaboration.

Three Pillars

The first pillar, Core Technology and Research Areas, will focus on Sports Analytics, DeepTech for Sports, Sports Biomechanics, Health and Life Sciences for Sports, and Sports Hardware and Electronics. These areas will explore the application of technology and research to sports performance, athlete assessment and the development of sports-related solutions.

The second pillar, Athlete Development, will encompass simulation and virtual training, injury prevention and rehabilitation, athlete well-being and psychology, talent identification, assistive technology, women in sports, coaching and capacity building. The focus will be on strengthening athlete development through technology-enabled interventions and specialised support.

The third pillar, Cross-Cutting Ecosystem Enablers, will include applied research and innovation, testing and validation, skilling, and institutional and industry collaboration, enabling partnerships and innovation across the SportsTech ecosystem.

The centre will be supported by the department through seed funding and infrastructure facilitation, while its operations will be led by professionals.

Definitive Agreements

Emphasising the proposed operating model, Kharge said the Centre would be “run by the industry, for the industry, for the sports fraternity.” The Minister said Karnataka has experience in establishing and operating industry-partnered Centres of Excellence, with more than 20 such centres in the state, including C-CAMP, Bengaluru Bioinnovation Centre, ARTpark and CISEC. He noted that these Centres have contributed to innovation and the creation of intellectual property, with the state’s Centres of Excellence having generated IP valued at over ₹13,000 crore.

The proposed centre will bring together industry and the sports fraternity to advance technology-led innovation in sports, building on Karnataka’s experience in industry-led Centres of Excellence. The structure, governance, roles, resources, commercial arrangements, timelines and specific deliverables of the proposed Centre will be mutually identified and formalised through subsequent definitive agreements, subject to the internal approvals of both parties.

The Letter of Intent is a non-binding expression of intent and does not create legal, financial, commercial, performance or timeline obligations on either party. The structure, governance, roles, resources, commercial arrangements, timelines and specific deliverables of the proposed Centre will be mutually identified and formalised through subsequent definitive agreements, subject to the internal approvals of both parties.

data.title: NETSCOUT’s Sustainability-by-Design Approach Combats Surging Data Center Energy Consumption
data.description:
NETSCOUT SYSTEMS, INC. (), a leading provider of network observability, AIOps, cybersecurity, and DDoS attack protection solutions, today announced that its approach to sustainable design is helping its customers achieve a 20% improvement in energy efficiency in their usage of NETSCOUT® products, reducing operating costs and environmental impact. The overall environmental impact could be further reduced depending upon the energy source utilized.

According to recent BloombergNEF research, global data center electricity demand will nearly quadruple by 2035 to 2,354 terawatt-hours, accounting for 7% of the global electricity demand. Forrester blogs note that resource optimization becomes everyone’s business: “Winners will not debate or care whether to label the response ‘sustainability.’ They will be forced to plan AI, energy, water, land, infrastructure, and community impact together, because that is now what resilient growth requires.”

NETSCOUT’s sustainability-by-design approach:

  • Prioritizes resource-efficient design at both the component and platform levels.

  • Helps organizations mitigate the environmental and financial impacts of rapidly increasing data center and AI energy consumption.

  • Enables upgrade of older devices with a single appliance to further optimize power efficiency.

Demonstrated Energy Savings
Performance lab testing of the InfiniStreamNG® 3U appliance measured the M-series platform versus the J-series. The results were reduced power consumption, yielding an estimated 1.3 MWh of annual energy savings per device. When cooling and power distribution losses are considered for the data center, power savings can be even higher. Similar results were observed in a live customer deployment.

"NETSCOUT's sustainability-by-design architectural approach means that we select for energy efficiency at the platform and component level," said Jillian James, director of sustainability, NETSCOUT. "We care about our customers' downstream energy and AI impact, not just our own footprint. Our intention is to help customers make their networks and analytics more resource-efficient and better for the environment."

Committed to Sustainability
The energy-efficient M-series platform reflects NETSCOUT’s broader corporate commitment to environmental responsibility. NETSCOUT is actively integrating sustainability into its operations and product development cycles to support circular economy principles. These product-level energy reductions are a key component of the company's ongoing progress toward its science-based greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for FY30.

By embedding energy efficiency into product design, NETSCOUT helps customers turn infrastructure modernization into lasting business value: lower operational costs, a smaller environmental impact, and greater capacity to support growing digital and AI demands. The M-series platform demonstrates how operational performance and sustainability can advance together, helping organizations make more effective use of power, space, and infrastructure investments. This approach enhances NETSCOUT’s value as resource efficiency becomes an increasingly important driver of technology purchasing decisions.

data.title: Europe Has 'Zero Interest' in Resuming Russian Gas Imports, U.S. Energy Chief Says — Update
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

WARSAW--European nations don't want to restart imports of Russian gas, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said, despite a spike in energy prices exacerbated by conflict in the Middle East.

"I've heard zero interest in going back," Wright said in reference to Europe resuming energy imports. He was speaking to the press at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation conference in Poland on Thursday.

The continent previously suffered from its reliance on Russian gas and is vocally resistant to resuming imports after they are phased out, Wright said.

Europe has been weaning itself off Russian energy imports since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine early in 2022. European Union legislation states that all purchases of Russian natural gas must be phased out by the end of 2027, and European leaders have opposed the full resumption of imports from a country they view as a strategic threat.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this month that a plan, broached by U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during trips to Moscow and Kyiv in September, would see Russian gas sold into Europe via a U.S. intermediary. The plan was later put on the back burner, but the potential for Russian gas to return to Europe hangs over the continent, the Journal reported.

Wright said he couldn't comment on discussions held by President Trump administration's about the possibility of Russian gas imports to Europe starting up again once the conflict ends.

The president is a "dealmaker and he's flexible" and will persevere with efforts to achieve peace between Russia and Ukraine, Wright said.

Poland has been one of the EU's most vocal members in its opposition to Russian gas returning to the continent. There can be no return to business as usual with Russia, the country's energy minister, Milosz Motyka, said Wednesday.

The conflict in the Middle East has upended energy markets this year, causing gas prices to soar and the prices of refined products like diesel and jet fuel to spike. Europe has been hit hard by the fresh rise in energy prices.

Wright acknowledged that there had been political pressure in the U.S. to stop or reduce exports of diesel, including to Europe, after prices soared to record levels.

"We did not do that. Energy is a globally traded commodity," he said. "The United States wants to be the reliable, forever supplier of energy to our allies around the world."
